title: Example Domains
text: Domains Protocols Numbers About Instructions and Guides Example Domains A number of domains such as example.com and example.org are maintained for documentation purposes. These domains may be used as illustrative examples in documents without prior coordination with us. They are not available for registration or transfer. We provide a web service on the example domain hosts to provide basic information on the purpose of the domain. These web services are provided as best effort, but are not designed to support production applications. We strongly recommend you do not design applications that require the example domains to have operating HTTP service. title: About us
text: Domains Protocols Numbers About About IANA For the Internet to work as a single seamless network, technical identifiers must mean the same thing everywhere: network identifiers like domain names and IP addresses must be assigned to a single party and have the same meaning globally, and communication protocols must use codes that have the same interpretation by every software implementation. The Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) maintains the authoritative public registries that record these allocations and definitions, providing a common global point of reference. Although the Internet is decentralized by design, a limited set of its technical elements require this globally coordinated administration. The IANA role is a public service. The registries we maintain are openly published, our services are provided without charge, and we act as a neutral steward implementing policies developed by the communities we serve. Much of our work involves processing requests for identifiers arising from technical standardization processes or submitted directly by users of IANA services. We assess each request carefully against the established policies governing the identifier’s allocation and use. Our responsibilities extend beyond maintaining the registries themselves. We also operate the systems used to publish the registries and their associated data, together with supporting operational services. These include infrastructure and events involved in producing, securing, and distributing key aspects of the DNS. The need for the IANA functions dates to the record-keeping activities that accompanied the earliest experiments leading to today’s Internet, and their origins can be traced to the 1970s. Today, the functions are performed by Public Technical Identifiers , a purpose-built affiliate of ICANN dedicated exclusively to delivering the IANA services. title: Archive
text: Domains Protocols Numbers About Archive These are archived documents from prior services, projects or oversight mechanism that are no longer active. These documents should not be relied upon for up-to-date information on operations and are provided for historical purposes only. A master index of all published reports is also available for perusal; individual reports are linked from the registries and pages to which they relate. Internet Monthly Reports 1991–1998 — Monthly status reports on Internet research and engineering activities, including IANA's reports to the research community. ccTLD News 1997–2003 — Memos sent to country-code top-level domain managers on policies, procedures and consultations of the day. NTIA Contract 2000–2016 — Documents relating to the United States Government contract for performance of the IANA functions, prior to the IANA stewardship transition. Initial Root DNSSEC Design and Launch 2008–2010 — Design documents, consultations and deployment materials from the project to first sign the DNS root zone. First KSK Rollover Project 2015–2018 — Planning and execution materials for the first rollover of the root zone key signing key.
